title: The 30% gap between planned merchandising and what's actually on shelves. — Trackeys

hero.h1: The 30% gap between planned merchandising and what's actually on shelves.
hero.p: Why store-level execution so often betrays brand-level strategy — and how to close the gap with measurement that doesn't rely on self-reporting.

sections.sub:
Almost every FMCG brand we benchmark has the same problem: what the trade marketing team plans and what the rep actually executes in-store diverge by an average of 30%. Sometimes more.
Planograms land in a rep's inbox as a PDF. The rep does their best. The auditor, weeks later, scores compliance from memory. Nobody is lying — the feedback loop is just too slow and fuzzy for anyone to act on.
Photo-based compliance scoring with the planogram visible on-screen. Real-time feedback to the rep. Aggregate dashboards that highlight the exact 3 stores out of 400 where compliance is slipping. That's enough to flip merchandising from a lagging audit to a leading signal.
